note.explanation: Enthalpy is the heat content of a system. The total enthalpy H cannot be measured directly, but the change in enthalpy, ΔH, can be measured. At constant pressure, ΔH equals the heat absorbed or evolved.
examples: If ΔH° = −566.0 kJ, the reaction is exothermic and gives 566.0 kJ of heat to the surroundings.
When heat enters or leaves a system, the system’s enthalpy changes.
note.checkAnswer: Enthalpy is the heat content of a system; enthalpy change is the difference in enthalpy when the system changes.
note.simple: Think of enthalpy as the energy content of a system. Heat is energy being transferred; that transfer can change the system’s enthalpy.

explain.title: Enthalpy and its symbol
explain.body: The total amount of heat energy present in a molecule under standard conditions (0°C temperature and 760 mm pressure) is also called its heat content. Enthalpy is the measurement of energy in a thermodynamic system. The quantity of enthalpy is equal to the total heat content of a system. Enthalpy of a system is represented by (H) while the change in enthalpy which a system undergoes is represented by ΔH.

explain.title: Total enthalpy and enthalpy change
explain.body: The total enthalpy (H) of a system cannot be measured directly. However, the change in enthalpy ΔH brought about in a system can be measured comparatively easily.

explain.title: Standard enthalpy of reaction
explain.body: In Chemistry, the standard enthalpy of reaction (ΔH°) is the enthalpy change when reactants in their standard states undergo reaction to produce products in their standard states. This quantity is called the standard enthalpy change or heat of reaction at constant pressure.

explain.title: Heat and enthalpy
explain.body: Heat is a form of energy that flows from hot body to a cold body because of a difference in temperature. We measure heat in joules. Heat is what we call the transfer of thermal energy. Enthalpy is an essential part of a system since it depends on the number of molecules present in that system, its chemical composition and its structure. When heat leaves or enters a system, it results in a change of enthalpy. At a constant pressure the enthalpy change is equal to heat evolved or absorbed.

mistakes: Do not treat heat and enthalpy as exactly the same thing: heat is energy in transfer, while enthalpy is a property of a system.
Do not confuse H, the enthalpy of a system, with ΔH, its enthalpy change.
Do not say the total enthalpy is measured directly; the textbook states that it cannot be measured directly.
Do not reverse the meaning of a negative ΔH: it means heat is given to the surroundings, so the reaction is exothermic.
